svg.title: Arrival and Spread of the Black Death Across Europe and Medieval Britain (1347–1350)
svg.desc: Two-panel historical GIS atlas map charting the arrival and spread of the Black Death (Yersinia pestis) from Genoese galleys at Messina, Genoa, and Marseille (Oct–Nov 1347) via Bordeaux and Calais (Spring 1348) to Melcombe Regis in Dorset (June 1348), Bristol (Aug 1348), London (Nov 1348), and across East Anglia, Wales, unpartitioned Ireland, York, and the Kingdom of Scotland (1349–1350).

text.tspan: Genoese Galleys Bring Plague from Caffa
Wine & Wool Cogs Sail to English Ports
First English Landfall • Gascon Trade Cog

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • PAPER 1 (OPTION 11): MEDICINE IN BRITAIN, c1250–PRESENT
Arrival & Spread of the Black Death: Europe to Medieval Britain (1347–50)
Maritime wool & wine cogs brought Yersinia pestis rats & fleas into Melcombe Regis (June 1348), killing 33%–50% of Britain by 1350.
Without Germ Theory, authorities blamed God’s wrath & miasma—ordering street-cleaning, prayers & bloodletting while fleas spread unchecked.
